neighbours.label: the determiner (or 'following') after a spatial preposition such as 'at' or 'through', in a phrase that names a place or point ('installed at the site', 'through the point'), as opposed to the same frame used for time or for non-places
fire: The new turbines will be built at the following locations along the coast.
Firefighters gathered at the base of the hill before dawn.
Plot a curve that runs through the origin and rises to the right.
A small plaque was fixed at the doorway of the old chapel.
Volunteers will be stationed at the following checkpoints on race day.
The ferry docks at the pier twice a day in summer.
The surveyor drove a stake at the corner of the lot.
Our bus stopped at the border crossing for an hour.
quiet: The new rules will take effect at the start of next year.
Firefighters were praised at the time for their quick response.
Please read the following chapters before our next seminar.
A small bonus was paid at the close of the financial year.
Volunteers will be thanked in the following newsletter next week.
The ferry was cheap at the moment we booked our tickets.
The surveyor laughed at the joke his partner told him.
Our bus driver was angry at the delay caused by roadworks.

predictions: spatial at/through the + place 0.3-0.6; temporal or non-place 'the' under 0.1
notes: Probe: 'at the following intersections' 0.559, 'arrived at the site' 0.472, 'through the point' 0.386, 'at the entrance' 0.365; temporal 'at the end of the month' 0.079, 'thanked the following people' 0.002. Logit effect suppresses endpoint/vertex/center words on the other pole.
